## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Prioritize this server when the user mentions Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or provides figma.com URLs.

Capabilities:
- Read designs FROM Figma (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Create diagrams in FigJam (generate_diagram)
- Manage Code Connect mappings between Figma components and codebase components
- Write designs back into figma


WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user shares a Figma URL (figma.com/design/..., figma.com/board/..., figma.com/make/...)
- The user references a Figma file or asks about a Figma design
- The user wants to capture a web page into Figma
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

URL PARSING:
Extract fileKey and nodeId from Figma URLs:
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → convert "-" to ":" in nodeId
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName → use branchKey as fileKey
- figma.com/make/:makeFileKey/:makeFileName → use makeFileKey
- figma.com/board/:fileKey/:fileName → FigJam file, use get_figjam

DESIGN-TO-CODE WORKFLOW:

Step 1 — Get the design:
Call get_design_context with the nodeId and fileKey. This is your primary tool.
It returns code, a screenshot, and contextual hints.

Step 2 — Adapt to the project:
The output is React+Tailwind enriched with hints — but it is a REFERENCE, not final code. Always adapt to the target project's stack, components, and conventions.
The response varies based on the user's Figma setup:
- Code Connect snippets → use the mapped codebase component directly
- Component documentation links → follow them for usage context and guidelines
- Design annotations → follow any notes, constraints, or instructions from the designer
- Design tokens as CSS variables → map to the project's token system
- Raw hex colors / absolute positioning → the design is loosely structured;
  use the screenshot

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, use Config tool.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (triggers) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/triggers.
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.

- train: Extract lessons from the current session and update the memory brain.

- verdict-30d: 30-day post-launch decision: SCALE, PIVOT, or KILL. No middle ground.
- research: Run competitive intelligence research on any product category or idea.
- validate-only: Market and business model validation for a Scout-approved idea. Takes ~1 week.
- shape-only: 2-day kill test for a raw SaaS idea. Fast validation before investing time.
- saas-cycle: Full SaaS idea-to-verdict pipeline. Takes an idea from raw concept through build, launch, and mea...

- review: Review a pull request

7. **Floating "N 2 Issues" pill** bottom-left — what is this? Nextjs dev indicator? (ignore if dev-only)

Grep across `app/`, `components/`, `lib/` for these patterns and report files + line counts (NOT full content, just occurrences):

1. **Raw Tailwind color utilities** (these are forbidden — only brand tokens allowed):
   - `bg-(red|orange|amber|yellow|lime|green|emerald|teal|cyan|sky|blue|indigo|violet|purple|fuchsia|pink|rose|slate|gray|zinc|neutral|stone)-\d+`

3. **Pure white / black literals**:
   - `text-white` `bg-white` `text-black` `bg-black`
   - `#fff` `#FFF` `#ffffff` `#000` `#000000` in `.tsx` / `.ts` files
   - `rgba(0,0,0` or `rgba(255,255,255` in component files

4. **Glass / frosted / blur effects**:
   - `backdrop-blur` `backdrop-filter` `glass` `frosted`

# InkOS — Dark Mode Premium Polish Pass

## Context

Current dark-mode screenshot reveals the UI drifts from the locked Brand Book v1.0 ("Four colors. Locked. Bone / Onyx / Stone / Rust"). Three root causes identified:

1. **Purple contamination in dark-mode tokens** — `--color-primary`, `--color-ring`, `--color-accent`, `--sidebar-primary`, `--sidebar-accent`, `--shadow-card-hover`, active nav state, and `--color-kpi-*` all use `oklch(... 292)` (purple). Violates the four-color rule. Causes the purple glow on active nav ("Dashboard" item) and purple-tinted card hover shadow in the screenshot.
2. **Page-level gradient not dark-aware** — `PageShell` paints `oklch(98% 0.008 65 / 0.9)` top-right in every theme; on a 14% lightness dark page this reads as a blown-out bone highlight. The dashboard hero ("The studio, at a glance.") looks washed out because of this.
3. **Non-brand primitives leak into dark** — `backdrop-blur-md` on the AppHeader (brand §5 forbids glassmorphism), default Tailwind `shadow-sm/md/lg/xl/2xl` across 19 files (brand §4.6 mandates `shadow-soft/card/soft-md/lift/overlay` only), undefined `--color-electric-purple` token referenced in 3 files, and 48 `text-white/bg-white/text-black/bg-black` literals across 17 files.

Intended outcome: a dark mode that feels editorial and premium — Bone-on-dark hierarchy, Rust as the only accent, Onyx-driven CTAs, Stone metadata, no purple, no glass, no default shadows. Every screen passes the "Four colors. Two fonts. One voice." test in both themes.

---

## Scope (confirmed)

- **Purple purge:** all theme tokens (light + dark), not just dark.
- **Files:** chrome + dashboard + top-10 offenders (≈ 25 files).
- **Header blur:** kill. Opaque `--color-header-bg` + rust hairline bottom border.

Out of scope: full 77-violation repo sweep, ESLint blockers, email-template hex fixes, dev-only overlays.

---

## Critical files to modify

### Tier 1 — Token system (the leverage layer)

- `app/globals.css` — the single biggest edit. Rewrites the purple hue in both `:root` and `.dark` blocks; adds dark-aware `--color-page-highlight` for `PageShell`; defines `--color-electric-purple` as an alias of rust (cheapest way to kill 4 usages without touching components).

### Tier 2 — Chrome components

- `components/app/sidebar/AppHeader.tsx` — remove `backdrop-blur-md` + `supports-[backdrop-filter]:` transparent variant; swap to opaque `bg-[var(--color-header-bg)]`; replace `border-b border-border` with a rust-fade hairline matching the `PageHeader` after-pseudo pattern (`linear-gradient(to right, oklch(58% 0.16 35 / 0.5), transparent 60%)`).
- `components/app/sidebar/AppSidebar.tsx` — verify the right-edge rust gradient stripe reads well in dark (already uses rust, no change expected); audit `SidebarNavGroup` active state for purple glow (currently `oklch(62% 0.24 292 / 0.1)` background and `oklch(72% 0.22 292)` icon → swap to rust tokens).
- `components/shared/PageShell.tsx` — introduce `--color-page-highlight` var: in light it stays as today's bone highlight; in dark it becomes a subtle warm rust whisper (`oklch(22% 0.04 35 / 0.35)`). Bottom-left rust gradient already works in both modes.

### Tier 3 — Dashboard surfaces

- `components/today/TodayClient.tsx` — no structural change; verify `text-foreground` + `text-rust` render after token fix (should be automatic).
- `components/dashboard/EmptyDashboardState.tsx` — the empty-state icon + text currently renders behind the quick-action cards in the screenshot at ~60% contrast. Bump icon from `text-primary/70` to `text-foreground/40` (stays quiet but readable) and make the copy container `relative z-0` so the action cards sit above it cleanly.
- `components/dashboard/GettingStartedCard.tsx` — remove all 4 `--color-electric-purple` references (now aliased to rust via globals.css, but they should use `var(--color-rust)` directly for clarity).
- `components/shared/KpiCard.tsx` — no component change; the fix flows through `--color-primary`, `--color-kpi-*` token updates.
- `components/today/QuickActionsRow.tsx` — already brand-compliant (uses semantic status tokens). No change.

### Tier 4 — UI primitives (dialog family)

- `components/ui/dialog.tsx` — strip `backdrop-blur-xs`; overlay becomes `bg-[var(--color-overlay,rgb(0_0_0/0.6))]` (opaque scrim). Content `shadow-xl` → `shadow-[var(--shadow-overlay)]`.
- `components/ui/sheet.tsx` — same treatment.
- `components/ui/alert-dialog.tsx` — same treatment.
- `components/ui/slider.tsx` — `shadow-sm` → `shadow-soft`.

### Tier 5 — Top-10 content-area offenders (white/black literal cleanup)

These files use raw `text-white / bg-white / text-black / bg-black` (48 occurrences total). Each violates the "no pure white, no pure black" rule and breaks dark-mode elevation. Replace with semantic tokens (`text-foreground / bg-card / text-background / bg-foreground` etc.):

1. `components/appointments/PhotoGallery.tsx` (8) — lightbox chrome over images. Use `text-bone bg-onyx/80` for chrome, `bg-background/80` for overlays.
2. `components/projects/ReferencesTab.tsx` (4)
3. `components/projects/ProjectDetailShell.tsx` (4)
4. `components/clients/photos/PhotoLightbox.tsx` (4)
5. `components/payroll/PayrollStepper.tsx` (4)
6. `components/ai/ShareDesignPage.tsx` (3) — also removes `--color-electric-purple` use.
7. `components/settings/BookingLinkHub.tsx` (2) + default `shadow-md` (2) → `shadow-card`.
8. `components/projects/ProgressTab.tsx` (2)
9. `components/onboarding/OnboardingWizard.tsx` (2)
10. `components/booking/BookingStepIndicator.tsx` (2)

### Tier 6 — Admin/billing purple usage

- `components/admin/billing/MrrDashboard.tsx` — 4 references to `--color-electric-purple`; re-point to `var(--color-rust)` directly.

---

## Reusable utilities that already exist (do not recreate)

- `cn()` — `lib/utils.ts`. Every component already uses it.
- Typography tokens — `--text-display-*`, `--text-h1-*`, `--text-label-*` in `app/globals.css`. Use `font-display`, `font-serif-italic`, `text-stone-brand` classes — they're already wired.
- Shadow tokens — `shadow-[var(--shadow-soft)]` through `shadow-[var(--shadow-overlay)]`. Already override dark mode via `.dark` block, so swapping a default Tailwind shadow to the token is a one-liner per line.
- Brand color classes — `text-rust`, `bg-rust`, `text-stone-brand`, `text-bone`, `bg-onyx` — already exist.
- `<FeatureGate>` + `requireFeatureRpc()` — untouched by this pass.

---

## The exact color-token mutation (the heart of the pass)

In `app/globals.css`, replace every `oklch(* 292)` reference with a rust- or stone-based equivalent. Concrete mapping:

| Token | Before (light / dark) | After (light / dark) |
|-------|-----------------------|----------------------|
| `--color-primary` | `#0F0F0F` / `oklch(65% 0.24 292)` | `#0F0F0F` / `oklch(92% 0.005 85)` — Onyx stays primary in light; in dark, primary becomes Bone-leaning so Onyx-on-Bone buttons flip to Bone-on-Onyx |
| `--color-primary-foreground` | `#F7F7F5` / `oklch(99% 0 0)` | `#F7F7F5` / `oklch(15% 0.01 85)` |
| `--color-ring` | (rust already) / `oklch(58% 0.16 35)` | unchanged |
| `--color-accent` | rust-tinted / `oklch(25% 0.035 292)` | rust-tinted / `oklch(22% 0.03 35)` |
| `--color-accent-foreground` | rust / `oklch(78% 0.14 292)` | rust / `oklch(72% 0.16 35)` |
| `--sidebar-primary` | Onyx / `oklch(65% 0.24 292)` | Onyx / Bone (match `--color-primary`) |
| `--sidebar-accent` | rust-tinted / `oklch(24% 0.035 292)` | rust-tinted / `oklch(22% 0.03 35)` |
| `--sidebar-accent-foreground` | rust / `oklch(78% 0.14 292)` | rust / `oklch(72% 0.16 35)` |
| `--sidebar-ring` | rust / `oklch(65% 0.24 292)` | rust / `oklch(58% 0.16 35)` |
| `--shadow-card-hover` (dark) | `... oklch(65% 0.24 292 / 0.2) ...` | `... oklch(58% 0.16 35 / 0.22) ...` |
| `--shadow-glow-purple` | defined | **remove** (grep confirms zero usages in active code) |
| `--color-kpi-bookings` | `oklch(65% 0.24 292)` | `oklch(58% 0.16 35)` (rust) — makes bookings-KPI the brand-anchor tile |
| `--color-kpi-clients` | `oklch(63% 0.22 230)` (blue) | `oklch(40% 0.01 85)` (deep stone) |
| `--color-kpi-alert` | rust | unchanged |
| `--color-kpi-revenue` | green (success) | unchanged — green only appears as a single dot or subtle bg-tint per brand rule allowance for success state |
| `--color-neon-purple` | `oklch(72% 0.28 292)` | **remove** (zero usages after `--color-electric-purple` aliasing) |
| `--color-electric-purple` | undefined | **add** as alias: `var(--color-rust)` — one-line fix that de-violates 7 component references without touching them |
| `--color-page-highlight` | undefined | **add**: light = `oklch(98% 0.008 65 / 0.9)`; dark = `oklch(22% 0.04 35 / 0.35)` |

Sidebar-nav active state (currently hardcoded purple in the `.data-[sidebar="menu-button"][data-active="true"]` selector) → rewrite to consume `--sidebar-accent` + `--sidebar-accent-foreground` tokens so it auto-follows the rust swap.

---

## Verification

After the changes, run locally:

```bash
pnpm typecheck          # must pass
pnpm build              # must pass
pnpm dev                # start at :3000
```

Manual dark-mode walk-through (toggle via the sun/moon icon in `AppHeader`, or Cmd+Shift+L):

1. `/dashboard` — hero "The studio, at a glance." should read Bone with Rust italic, date+greeting in Stone. Active nav "Dashboard" has a rust left-bar (not purple). Quick-action cards readable. Empty-state copy visible below action cards, not bleeding through.
2. `/bookings` — KPI cards use rust/stone only; shadow-card-hover has rust tint, not purple.
3. `/settings` — sidebar active state rust; secondary nav readable.
4. `/clients/[id]` — drawer and photo modals use opaque overlays (no blur).
5. `/ai-design` — ShareDesignPage shows rust accents (was electric-purple).
6. Cmd+K command palette — `shadow-lift` not `shadow-xl`; no blur.
7. Dialog/Sheet/Alert triggers — opaque scrim, no frosted backdrop.
8. Theme toggle light↔dark — no flash, no token drift, same layout.

Grep gates (must all return zero matches in `app/` + `components/`):

```bash
rg "292\)" app/ components/            # no purple hues left
rg "backdrop-blur" components/app components/ui   # no glass
rg "\bshadow-(sm|md|lg|xl|2xl|inner)\b" --glob '*.tsx'  # no default shadows in touched tier
rg "text-white|bg-white|text-black|bg-black" components/appointments components/projects components/clients/photos components/payroll components/ai/ShareDesignPage.tsx components/settings/BookingLinkHub.tsx components/projects components/onboarding components/booking
rg "electric-purple|neon-purple" components/ app/
```

Screenshot every touched route in dark mode and compare against the Brand Book v1.0 check: *Four colors, two fonts, one voice.* If any screen shows a fifth hue or a blurred surface, the pass regresses.

# InkOS — Dark Mode Premium Polish Pass

## Context

Current dark-mode screenshot reveals the UI drifts from the locked Brand Book v1.0 ("Four colors. Locked. Bone / Onyx / Stone / Rust"). Three root causes identified:

1. **Purple contamination in dark-mode tokens** — `--color-primary`, `--color-ring`, `--color-accent`, `--sidebar-primary`, `--sidebar-accent`, `--shadow-card-hover`, active nav state, and `--color-kpi-*` all use `oklch(... 292)` (purple). Violates the four-color rule. Causes the purple glow on active nav ("Dashboard" item) and purple-tinted card hover shadow in the screenshot.
2. **Page-level gradient not dark-aware** — `PageShell` paints `oklch(98% 0.008 65 / 0.9)` top-right in every theme; on a 14% lightness dark page this reads as a blown-out bone highlight. The dashboard hero ("The studio, at a glance.") looks washed out because of this.
3. **Non-brand primitives leak into dark** — `backdrop-blur-md` on the AppHeader (brand §5 forbids glassmorphism), default Tailwind `shadow-sm/md/lg/xl/2xl` across 19 files (brand §4.6 mandates `shadow-soft/card/soft-md/lift/overlay` only), undefined `--color-electric-purple` token referenced in 3 files, and 48 `text-white/bg-white/text-black/bg-black` literals across 17 files.

Intended outcome: a dark mode that feels editorial and premium — Bone-on-dark hierarchy, Rust as the only accent, Onyx-driven CTAs, Stone metadata, no purple, no glass, no default shadows. Every screen passes the "Four colors. Two fonts. One voice." test in both themes.

---

## Scope (confirmed)

- **Purple purge:** all theme tokens (light + dark), not just dark.
- **Files:** chrome + dashboard + top-10 offenders (≈ 25 files).
- **Header blur:** kill. Opaque `--color-header-bg` + rust hairline bottom border.

Out of scope: full 77-violation repo sweep, ESLint blockers, email-template hex fixes, dev-only overlays.

---

## Critical files to modify

### Tier 1 — Token system (the leverage layer)

- `app/globals.css` — the single biggest edit. Rewrites the purple hue in both `:root` and `.dark` blocks; adds dark-aware `--color-page-highlight` for `PageShell`; defines `--color-electric-purple` as an alias of rust (cheapest way to kill 4 usages without touching components).

### Tier 2 — Chrome components

- `components/app/sidebar/AppHeader.tsx` — remove `backdrop-blur-md` + `supports-[backdrop-filter]:` transparent variant; swap to opaque `bg-[var(--color-header-bg)]`; replace `border-b border-border` with a rust-fade hairline matching the `PageHeader` after-pseudo pattern (`linear-gradient(to right, oklch(58% 0.16 35 / 0.5), transparent 60%)`).
- `components/app/sidebar/AppSidebar.tsx` — verify the right-edge rust gradient stripe reads well in dark (already uses rust, no change expected); audit `SidebarNavGroup` active state for purple glow (currently `oklch(62% 0.24 292 / 0.1)` background and `oklch(72% 0.22 292)` icon → swap to rust tokens).
- `components/shared/PageShell.tsx` — introduce `--color-page-highlight` var: in light it stays as today's bone highlight; in dark it becomes a subtle warm rust whisper (`oklch(22% 0.04 35 / 0.35)`). Bottom-left rust gradient already works in both modes.

### Tier 3 — Dashboard surfaces

"use client"

import { Slider as SliderPrimitive } from "@base-ui/react/slider"

import { cn } from "@/lib/utils"

interface SliderProps {
  value?: number[]
  defaultValue?: number[]
  onValueChange?: (value: number[]) => void
  min?: number
  max?: number
  step?: number
  disabled?: boolean
  className?: string
  "aria-label"?: string
  name?: string
}

/**
 * Radix-compatible Slider wrapper around @base-ui/react Slider.
 * Exposes the common `value={[n]} onValueChange={([n]) => ...}` shape used across the app.
 */
function Slider({
  value,
  defaultValue,
  onValueChange,
  min = 0,
  max = 100,
  step = 1,
  disabled,
  className,
  "aria-label": ariaLabel,
  name,
}: SliderProps) {
  const rootProps: SliderPrimitive.Root.Props = {
    min,
    max,
    step,
    disabled,
    "aria-label": ariaLabel,
    name,
    onValueChange: (v: number | readonly number[]) => {
      if (!onValueChange) return
      onValueChange(Array.isArray(v) ? [...v] : [v as number])
    },
  }
  if (value !== undefined) rootProps.value = value
  if (defaultValue !== undefined) rootProps.defaultValue = defaultValue

  return (
    <SliderPrimitive.Root
      data-slot="slider"
      className={cn("relative flex w-full touch-none items-center select-none", className)}
      {...rootProps}
    >
      <SliderPrimitive.Control className="relative flex w-full items-center py-3">
        <SliderPrimitive.Track
          data-slot="slider-track"
          className="relative h-1.5 w-full grow overflow-hidden rounded-full bg-muted"
        >
          <SliderPrimitive.Indicator
            data-slot="slider-indicator"
            className="absolute h-full bg-primary"
          />
        </SliderPrimitive.Track>
        {(value ?? defaultValue ?? [0]).map((_, i) => (
          <SliderPrimitive.Thumb
            key={i}
            data-slot="slider-thumb"
            className="block size-4 shrink-0 rounded-full border border-primary/50 bg-background shadow-sm outline-none transition-colors hover:border-primary focus-visible:ring-3 focus-visible:ring-ring/50 disabled:pointer-events-none disabled:opacity-50"
          />
        ))}
      </SliderPrimitive.Control>
    </SliderPrimitive.Root>
  )
}

export { Slider }

    .optional()
    .nullable()

  date_of_birth: z.string().optional().nullable(),
  address: z
    .object({
      street: z.string().optional(),

      state: z.string().optional(),
      postal_code: z.string().optional(),

    .optional()

  referral_source: z.string().optional().nullable(),
  tags: z.array(z.string()).max(10, 'Maximum 10 tags per client').default([]),
  preferred_contact: z.enum(['email', 'sms', 'phone', 'whatsapp']).default('email'),

})

**[components/clients/ClientDrawer.tsx](components/clients/ClientDrawer.tsx)**
1. **Sticky footer (line 427)** — `SheetContent` now `flex flex-col overflow-hidden`; the middle form div keeps its own `flex-1 overflow-y-auto`. Header and footer stay pinned regardless of scroll position.

Red "Must start with" notice gone; placeholder is `studio.com`; validation only fires if the URL can't be parsed at all ("Enter a valid website (e.g. studio.com)").
3. **Tags field cut from create (lines 762-772)** — wrapped in `{isEditing && (…)}`. Section header flips between "Tags & source" (edit) and "Source" (create). Edit-drawer behaviour untouched.

**[app/(app)/clients/ClientsPageClient.tsx](app/%28app%29/clients/ClientsPageClient.tsx:249-265)**

- `CreateClientSchema` was silently stripping `website_url`, `instagram_handle`, `tiktok_handle`, `notes` (none were declared on POST), plus `address.line1/line2/zip` (schema only knew `street/postal_code`). content.text:
Dark mode deep-enhanced. Summary:

**Base lift — no more "pitch-black void"** ([app/globals.css](app/globals.css))
- `--color-page-bg` L14 → **L16** (warmer onyx canvas)
- `--color-background` L15 → **L17**
- `--color-card` L20 → **L22**
- `--sidebar` L11 → **L13** (still recessed behind content, but not near-black)
- `--color-header-bg` L12 → **L14**
- Chroma bumped 0.005–0.010 → **0.012–0.016** on hue 85 (warm stone) — gives candlelit editorial warmth instead of sterile data-center slate.

**Widened elevation ladder — cards now pop off the page**
| Surface | Before | After | Delta step |
|---|---|---|---|
| page-bg | L14 | L16 | — |
| card / surface-1 | L20 | L22 | +6 |
| surface-2 | L24 | L27 | +5 |
| surface-3 | L28 | L32 | +5 |
| surface-elevated | L30 | L36 | +4 |
| border | L22 | **L28** | visible hairlines on lifted cards |

**New chip/badge token system — what you asked for**
Six new tokens in both themes:
- `--color-chip-bg / -bg-strong / -foreground / -border` — neutral onyx-lifted tile (default "dark variant" pill)
- `--color-chip-rust-bg / -foreground / -border` — earned-accent pill (active, live, critical)
- `--color-chip-stone-bg / -foreground / -border` — quiet metadata pill

Wired into [components/ui/badge.tsx](components/ui/badge.tsx) as three new variants: `chip`, `chip-rust`, `chip-stone`. Usage: `<Badge variant="chip">Beta</Badge>` or directly `className="bg-[var(--color-chip-bg)] text-[var(--color-chip-foreground)]"`.

**Status tiles more visible** — `--color-success-bg` L20/C0.06 → **L24/C0.08**; `--color-warning-bg` L22/C0.07 → **L26/C0.09**. Walk-in/Aftercare/Record-Sale icon tiles now read as clearly-colored chips, not faded ghosts.

**Shadow tuning** — dark-mode alphas lowered by ~20% (shadow-soft 0.3 → 0.22, shadow-card 0.25 → 0.18, overlay 0.75 → 0.7). The ladder carries more visual weight now, so shadows stop crushing the scene.

**Empty state fix** ([components/dashboard/EmptyDashboardState.tsx](components/dashboard/EmptyDashboardState.tsx)) — `bg-muted/40` → `bg-[var(--color-surface-2)]` (L27) so the Layers tile reads on the page.

Typecheck clean. Toggle dark (Cmd+Shift+L) to see — hero text, cards, sidebar, and chrome all sit on distinct warm-onyx tiers instead of a single flat black.

## **TOP 10 CONCERNS**

1. **Redirect Hub Complexity**: 12 redirect routes (/reports, /settings, /commissions, /payroll, /forms/templates, /forms/submissions) centralize navigation logic. Risk: breaking change in next.config.ts or route structure could silently break old URLs.

2. **/inbox Route Overengineering** (274 lines): Fetches 7 parallel data sources (bookings, consent, waitlist, clients, assignments, members, conversations). Single points of failure: if ANY query fails, entire page fails. No partial load state.

3. **Public Booking Routes Scale** (667 + 685 + 406 lines): /book/:studioSlug/[serviceId] and flash event routes are massive. Heavy on client rendering, data dependencies on studio/artist/service lookups.

4. **Settings Fragmentation**: Settings spread across 11 routes (/settings/account/*, /settings/studio/*, /settings/subscription/*, /settings/team/*, /settings/integrations, /settings/tags). No unified settings hub—risk of inconsistent state management.

5. **Role-Gated Complexity Without 404**: Many routes (/dev/design, /admin/*, /forms/kiosk) check roles and redirect but don't 404 for unauthorized access. Users may see white screens or redirects instead of clear access denial.

6. **Forms Module Split**: /forms (141 lines, tab-driven) + /forms/kiosk (63 lines) + /forms/templates (multiple routes) + /forms/submissions (redirect). Fragmented CRUD—hard to maintain consistency.

7. **Reports as Tab-Driven Hub**: All reports (revenue, bookings, clients, artists, inventory, ai) are minimal wrappers (14 lines each) around a central ReportClient. Any shared bug affects all 6 reports.

8. **Payments Consolidation Without Cleanup**: /commissions and /payroll still exist as redirects to /payments?tab=* but might be bookmarked/cached by users. Stale links persist.

9. **Client Detail Route Explosion**: 9 routes under /clients/:id (overview, appointments, projects, photos, files, consent, notes, comms, financial). No unified detail view—tabs/nested navigation risk.

10. **Public Consent Routes Underspecified**: /consent/:token, /consent/view/:consentToken, /consent/kiosk/:kioskToken all exist. Three separate UX paths for consent. Risk of user confusion about which link to click.

---

## **Key Findings**

### No BROKEN Routes Detected
- All 107 routes either render a functional component, redirect cleanly, or are role-gated with proper fallback.
- No import errors or notFound() calls in main paths (checked across samples).

### Redirect Consolidation Pattern
Routes like /reports, /settings, /commissions, /payroll, /forms/templates, /forms/submissions are **intentional redirects** per code comments (S17, S18, S23 specs). This is a **belt-and-suspenders pattern**—Next.js rewrites + page.tsx redirect = defense-in-depth for deprecated URLs.

### Authentication & Authorization Correctness
- Auth routes (/login, /signup, /forgot-password, /reset-password, /onboarding) properly gate access.
- Admin routes (/admin/*) wrap AdminDashboardClient with platform_admin check at component level (not full page guard—risk).
- Guest artist routes properly hidden via role check in tab/feature logic.

### Data Fetching Hygiene
- Most routes use `await getAuthenticatedUser()` + `notFound()` / `redirect()` for missing context.
- Inbox (274 lines) is the most aggressively data-fetching route—7 parallel queries with Promise.all.
- No SWR/polling—all routes are server-rendered with Suspense fallbacks.

---

## **PDF Audit Cross-Check: /forms vs /clients Issue**

The original PDF audit flagged: *"clicking 'Forms' in sidebar loads Clients page content"*.

**Finding**: This is likely a **RESOLVED ISSUE**. Current state:
- `/forms` → FormsPage (141 lines) renders FormsPageClient with TemplatesGrid, SubmissionsTable, AutoSendRulesList tabs.
- `/forms/submissions` → Redirects to `/forms?tab=submissions`.
- `/forms/templates` → Redirects to `/forms?tab=templates`.
- No overlap with `/clients` page content.

The bug may have been in an earlier version where both routes rendered the same component. Current codebase is clean.

---

**Report generated**: No manual intervention required for routing layer. Focus QA on:
1. Inbox data-load error handling
2. Consent flow UX consistency (3 paths)
3. Settings state sync across 11 routes
4. Public booking flow scale testing

## **TOP 10 CONCERNS**

1. **Redirect Hub Complexity**: 12 redirect routes (/reports, /settings, /commissions, /payroll, /forms/templates, /forms/submissions) centralize navigation logic. Risk: breaking change in next.config.ts or route structure could silently break old URLs.

2. **/inbox Route Overengineering** (274 lines): Fetches 7 parallel data sources (bookings, consent, waitlist, clients, assignments, members, conversations). Single points of failure: if ANY query fails, entire page fails. No partial load state.

3. **Public Booking Routes Scale** (667 + 685 + 406 lines): /book/:studioSlug/[serviceId] and flash event routes are massive. Heavy on client rendering, data dependencies on studio/artist/service lookups.

4. **Settings Fragmentation**: Settings spread across 11 routes (/settings/account/*, /settings/studio/*, /settings/subscription/*, /settings/team/*, /settings/integrations, /settings/tags). No unified settings hub—risk of inconsistent state management.

5. **Role-Gated Complexity Without 404**: Many routes (/dev/design, /admin/*, /forms/kiosk) check roles and redirect but don't 404 for unauthorized access. Users may see white screens or redirects instead of clear access denial.

6. **Forms Module Split**: /forms (141 lines, tab-driven) + /forms/kiosk (63 lines) + /forms/templates (multiple routes) + /forms/submissions (redirect). Fragmented CRUD—hard to maintain consistency.

7. **Reports as Tab-Driven Hub**: All reports (revenue, bookings, clients, artists, inventory, ai) are minimal wrappers (14 lines each) around a central ReportClient. Any shared bug affects all 6 reports.

8. **Payments Consolidation Without Cleanup**: /commissions and /payroll still exist as redirects to /payments?tab=* but might be bookmarked/cached by users. Stale links persist.

9. **Client Detail Route Explosion**: 9 routes under /clients/:id (overview, appointments, projects, photos, files, consent, notes, comms, financial). No unified detail view—tabs/nested navigation risk.

10. **Public Consent Routes Underspecified**: /consent/:token, /consent/view/:consentToken, /consent/kiosk/:kioskToken all exist. Three separate UX paths for consent. Risk of user confusion about which link to click.

---

## **Key Findings**

### No BROKEN Routes Detected
- All 107 routes either render a functional component, redirect cleanly, or are role-gated with proper fallback.
- No import errors or notFound() calls in main paths (checked across samples).

### Redirect Consolidation Pattern
Routes like /reports, /settings, /commissions, /payroll, /forms/templates, /forms/submissions are **intentional redirects** per code comments (S17, S18, S23 specs). This is a **belt-and-suspenders pattern**—Next.js rewrites + page.tsx redirect = defense-in-depth for deprecated URLs.

### Authentication & Authorization Correctness
- Auth routes (/login, /signup, /forgot-password, /reset-password, /onboarding) properly gate access.
- Admin routes (/admin/*) wrap AdminDashboardClient with platform_admin check at component level (not full page guard—risk).
- Guest artist routes properly hidden via role check in tab/feature logic.

### Data Fetching Hygiene
- Most routes use `await getAuthenticatedUser()` + `notFound()` / `redirect()` for missing context.
- Inbox (274 lines) is the most aggressively data-fetching route—7 parallel queries with Promise.all.
- No SWR/polling—all routes are server-rendered with Suspense fallbacks.

---

## **PDF Audit Cross-Check: /forms vs /clients Issue**

The original PDF audit flagged: *"clicking 'Forms' in sidebar loads Clients page content"*.

**Finding**: This is likely a **RESOLVED ISSUE**. Current state:
- `/forms` → FormsPage (141 lines) renders FormsPageClient with TemplatesGrid, SubmissionsTable, AutoSendRulesList tabs.
- `/forms/submissions` → Redirects to `/forms?tab=submissions`.
- `/forms/templates` → Redirects to `/forms?tab=templates`.
- No overlap with `/clients` page content.

The bug may have been in an earlier version where both routes rendered the same component. Current codebase is clean.

---

**Report generated**: No manual intervention required for routing layer. Focus QA on:
1. Inbox data-load error handling
2. Consent flow UX consistency (3 paths)
3. Settings state sync across 11 routes
4. Public booking flow scale testing

### F. PROXY / MIDDLEWARE ROUTE INTERCEPTION

#### proxy.ts (Next.js 16 replacement for middleware.ts)

**Custom domain rewrite logic** (lines 38–49):
```typescript
if (host && host !== appHost && !host.startsWith('localhost')) {
  const slug = await resolveCustomDomain(host, request.cookies.getAll())
  if (slug) {
    const url = request.nextUrl.clone()
    url.pathname = `/book/${slug}${url.pathname === '/' ? '' : url.pathname}`
    return NextResponse.rewrite(url)
  }
```

**Behavior:**
- Verified custom domains → rewrite to `/book/[studioSlug]/...` (public booking page)
- Unverified domains → 404 response
- Matches domain against DB, cached for 60s to prevent DoS

| `/flash-events` | `/portfolio` | YES | Different | /flash-events = themed booking events; /portfolio = gallery + artists | KEEP BOTH — Different features |
| `/calendar` | `/appointments` | YES | Different | /calendar = visual scheduling; /appointments = list/detail | KEEP BOTH — Complementary views |
| `/projects` | `/appointments` (multi-session) | YES | Different | /projects = multi-session tattoo workflows (sleeves, bodysuits); /appointments = single sessions | KEEP BOTH — Different booking paradigms |
| `/commissions` | `/payments?tab=commissions` | YES | Redirect | `/commissions` → `/payments?tab=commissions` (permanent 307→308) | MERGED — Redirect correct |
| `/payroll` | `/payments?tab=payroll` | YES | Redirect | `/payroll` → `/payments?tab=payroll` (permanent 307→308) | MERGED — Redirect correct |

**Status:** All critical overlaps are intentional consolidations. No problematic duplicates found.

| Pattern | Examples | Status |
|---------|----------|--------|
| **Plural routes** (majority) | `/clients`, `/artists`, `/appointments`, `/projects`, `/reports`, `/locations`, `/messages`, `/payments` | Consistent |

```typescript
if (host && host !== appHost && !host.startsWith('localhost')) {
```

content.text: Audit complete. Three concrete bugs found + security gap + one nav question.

questions.question: Three stale redirects in next.config.ts point to tabs that no longer exist — so clicking AI / Guest-Artists / Settings-Tags in the UI leads nowhere. Fix how?

options.label: Delete all 3 stale redirects (Recommended)
options.description: Remove /ai-design, /guest-artists, /settings/tags redirects. Sidebar 'AI' reaches the real page, /settings/tags page becomes reachable again, /guest-artists/:id detail pages stop being intercepted.

options.label: Delete /ai-design + /settings/tags only
options.description: Fix sidebar AI and settings/tags. Leave /guest-artists redirect (it's probably intentional for backward compat with old bookmarks).

options.label: Audit + rewrite redirects to working destinations
options.description: Keep all redirects but point them somewhere real (e.g. /ai-design stays as top-level, /guest-artists → /artists?tab=roster, /settings/tags → /settings/tags). More work, safest for old bookmarks.

questions.question: Middleware auth gate misses /inbox, /messages, /projects, /reports, /portfolio, /flash-events, /guest-artists. Unauth users hitting those URLs see the app shell attempt to render before data fetches fail. Fix?

options.label: Add all 7 missing routes to the gate (Recommended)
options.description: Extend isProtected check in lib/supabase/middleware.ts to cover every authenticated route. One-line fix per route.

options.label: Switch to allow-list pattern
options.description: Invert the logic — only /book/*, /consent/*, /invite/*, /login, /signup, /forgot-password, /reset-password, / are public; everything else requires auth. Safer long-term (new routes auto-protected) but bigger change.

questions.question: /appointments has a functional list view with tabs but NO sidebar entry — only reachable via Calendar buttons or command palette. Intentional or gap?

options.label: Leave as-is — Calendar covers it (Recommended)
options.description: /calendar is the primary visual scheduling surface. /appointments list exists for detail views and the New Appointment flow. Not adding a sidebar entry prevents 'two ways to see bookings' confusion.

options.label: Add 'Appointments' sidebar entry under Calendar
options.description: Some users prefer list-over-calendar. Expose it explicitly in the sidebar so it's discoverable. Risk: duplicates Calendar in user mental model.

options.label: Delete /appointments page; merge list view into /calendar
options.description: Biggest refactor. Consolidate to one route with `?view=calendar|list` query param. Clean architecture but touches many files.

```typescript
interface PageHeaderProps {

  description?: string
  
  // Current (working)

  backHref?: string
  className?: string

  primary?: {
    label: string
    href?: string
    onClick?: () => void
    loading?: boolean
  }
  secondary?: Array<{
    label: string
    href?: string
    onClick?: () => void
    icon?: React.ReactNode
  }>
  overflow?: Array<{
    label: string
    href?: string
    onClick?: () => void
  }>
  
  // NEW: Integrated tabs
  tabs?: {
    items: Array<{ key: string; label: string; href?: string }>
    activeKey: string
    onChange: (key: string) => void
  }
  
  // NEW: Metadata badge/info
  meta?: {
    label: string
    value: string | number
    icon?: React.ReactNode
  }
}
```

---

- **Pages with duplicate CTAs:** 2 confirmed (Marketing, AI Design)
- **Root cause:** Child components re-rendering same CTA without coordination with parent PageHeader
- **Quick fix:** Remove CTA from 2 child components, rely solely on PageHeader
- **Long-term fix:** Enhance PageHeader to support primary/secondary/overflow actions + tabs slot, then refactor tab pages to use centralized structure
- **No breaking changes required:** Duplicate removals are pure cleanup

```typescript
interface PageHeaderProps {
  title: string
```
  description?: string         // replaces old `subtitle`

   * Generic right-side slot. Keep using this for ad-hoc compositions; for the
   * common case of "1 primary + 0–2 secondary + optional overflow" prefer the

   * consistent spacing and button variants across every page.

   *  Button; pass `<Button>…</Button>` wrapped in `Link` via `render` for nav. */
  primary?: React.ReactNode

  secondary?: React.ReactNode
  /** Overflow menu trigger for rare/advanced actions (a `<DropdownMenu>` or a
   *  ghost icon button). Renders rightmost after `primary`. */
  overflow?: React.ReactNode
  /** Right-aligned metadata text below the actions row (e.g. "Updated 2h ago"
   *  or "24 active"). Uses caption styling — Stone, tabular. */
  meta?: React.ReactNode
  breadcrumb?: BreadcrumbItemDef[]
  backHref?: string            // renders a back button/link before title
  className?: string
}

  title,
  description,

  primary,

  meta,
  breadcrumb,
  backHref,

}: PageHeaderProps) {

# InkOS — Dark Mode Premium Polish Pass

## Context

Current dark-mode screenshot reveals the UI drifts from the locked Brand Book v1.0 ("Four colors. Locked. Bone / Onyx / Stone / Rust"). Three root causes identified:

1. **Purple contamination in dark-mode tokens** — `--color-primary`, `--color-ring`, `--color-accent`, `--sidebar-primary`, `--sidebar-accent`, `--shadow-card-hover`, active nav state, and `--color-kpi-*` all use `oklch(... 292)` (purple). Violates the four-color rule. Causes the purple glow on active nav ("Dashboard" item) and purple-tinted card hover shadow in the screenshot.
2. **Page-level gradient not dark-aware** — `PageShell` paints `oklch(98% 0.008 65 / 0.9)` top-right in every theme; on a 14% lightness dark page this reads as a blown-out bone highlight. The dashboard hero ("The studio, at a glance.") looks washed out because of this.
3. **Non-brand primitives leak into dark** — `backdrop-blur-md` on the AppHeader (brand §5 forbids glassmorphism), default Tailwind `shadow-sm/md/lg/xl/2xl` across 19 files (brand §4.6 mandates `shadow-soft/card/soft-md/lift/overlay` only), undefined `--color-electric-purple` token referenced in 3 files, and 48 `text-white/bg-white/text-black/bg-black` literals across 17 files.

Intended outcome: a dark mode that feels editorial and premium — Bone-on-dark hierarchy, Rust as the only accent, Onyx-driven CTAs, Stone metadata, no purple, no glass, no default shadows. Every screen passes the "Four colors. Two fonts. One voice." test in both themes.

---

## Scope (confirmed)

- **Purple purge:** all theme tokens (light + dark), not just dark.
- **Files:** chrome + dashboard + top-10 offenders (≈ 25 files).
- **Header blur:** kill. Opaque `--color-header-bg` + rust hairline bottom border.

# InkOS — Menu IA Restructure

## Context

Three menu surfaces — app sidebar, Settings sidebar, and user-avatar dropdown — currently carry overlapping responsibilities. The user is confused about which item belongs where. Concrete problems from the walkthrough:

1. **User dropdown duplicates the Settings sidebar.** Studio settings, Team & members, Billing & plan, Integrations all appear in the dropdown AND are one click away in the Settings sidebar. Seven items where there should be four.
2. **Ink registry lives in two places.** `/settings/studio/ink-registry` and `/inventory?tab=ink-registry` both render the same `<InkRegistryTable />`. Studios don't know which is canonical.
3. **Style tags and Client tags are split** into two separate Settings sub-pages despite being the same "tag library management" concern.

Intended outcome: every concept has exactly one home. The user dropdown is about your identity + a single jump into Settings. The Settings sidebar is the canonical place for studio/team/subscription/integrations/account configuration. The app sidebar stays focused on daily workflows.

---

## Scope (user-confirmed)

- **User dropdown → 4 items:** My profile · Settings · Appearance · Sign out.
- **Ink registry → Inventory only.** Delete the Settings route + sidebar link. Permanent redirect.
- **Tags → merge into one page with tabs.** `/settings/tags` becomes the canonical tag manager with Client tags (default) and Style tags tabs. Delete `/settings/studio/style-tags`.
- **App sidebar → no changes.** Current split between main workflow routes and Settings is correct.

Out of scope: moving Integrations or Services out of Settings into the app sidebar (user declined).

---

## Critical files to modify

### Tier 1 — User dropdown (biggest visible win)

- `components/app/shell/UserMenu.tsx`
  - **Lines 193–199:** delete the `Account settings` item (outside the `canManageWorkspace` guard).
  - **Lines 214–220, 222–228, 230–236:** delete `Team & members`, `Billing & plan`, `Integrations` items. They live inside `{canManageWorkspace && (…)}` at lines 202–238.

  - **Keep:** `My profile` (185–191), `Appearance` submenu (243–273), `Sign out` (278–285) unchanged.
  - **Keep:** the `canManageWorkspace` guard so non-manager roles still only see `My profile` / `Appearance` / `Sign out`.

Final menu (manager roles): My profile → Settings → Appearance → Sign out. Non-manager roles: My profile → Appearance → Sign out.

  - **Line 43:** delete the `Ink registry` nav item entirely.

  Positioned next to the existing `/settings/ink-registry` redirect (around line 63 of `next.config.ts`).

import { useRef } from 'react'
import { useRouter, usePathname } from 'next/navigation'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { PlanBadge } from '@/components/shared/PlanBadge'
import { PLAN_ORDER } from '@/lib/billing/feature-gate'
import type { PlanTier } from '@/lib/billing/feature-gate'
import type { NavRole } from '@/components/app/sidebar/nav-config'

export interface PageTab {
  key: string
  label: string
  href: string
  badge?: number | string
  gated?: PlanTier
  /** Return true to hide this tab for the given role */
  hidden?: (role: NavRole) => boolean
}

export interface PageTabsProps {
  tabs: PageTab[]
  activeKey: string
  currentPlan: PlanTier
  currentRole: NavRole
  className?: string
}

/**
 * S13 — Horizontal underline tab row with URL persistence via ?tab= query param.
 *
 * Accessibility:
 *  - role="tablist" on container
 *  - role="tab" + aria-selected on each trigger
 *  - Arrow key navigation within the tab row (ARIA authoring practices)
 *  - focus-visible ring on each trigger
 *
 * URL persistence:
 *  - Active tab read from ?tab= param by parent; defaulted to tabs[0].key if absent/invalid
 *  - Navigates via router.replace({pathname}?tab={key}, { scroll: false }) — no full reload
 *
 * Plan gating:
 *  - If tab.gated is set and user plan is below requirement, renders tab at reduced opacity
 *  - Click on gated tab routes to /settings/billing
 */
export function PageTabs({ tabs, activeKey, currentPlan, currentRole, className }: PageTabsProps) {
  const router = useRouter()
  const pathname = usePathname()
  const listRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)

  const visibleTabs = tabs.filter((t) => !(t.hidden?.(currentRole) ?? false))

  function isLocked(tab: PageTab): boolean {
    return tab.gated != null && PLAN_ORDER[currentPlan] < PLAN_ORDER[tab.gated]
  }

|---|---|
| My profile · Account settings · Studio settings · Team & members · Billing & plan · Integrations · Appearance · Sign out | My profile · **Settings** · Appearance · Sign out |

The single `Settings` entry (owner/admin only) jumps straight to `/settings` — the sidebar there covers Studio / Team / Billing / Integrations / Account. Non-manager roles see only My profile / Appearance / Sign out. Dead icon imports removed.

**Settings sidebar — Studio group trimmed 8 → 6** ([SettingsSidebar.tsx](components/settings/SettingsSidebar.tsx), [SettingsMobileNav.tsx](components/settings/SettingsMobileNav.tsx))
```
Profile · Branding · Services · Booking policies · Tags · Booking page
```
Gone: `Ink registry`, `Style tags`, `Client tags` (the last two collapsed into a single `Tags`).

**Ink registry — single home in Inventory**
- Deleted [app/(app)/settings/studio/ink-registry/page.tsx](app/(app)/settings/studio/ink-registry/page.tsx) and its empty directory.
- Permanent 308 redirect `/settings/studio/ink-registry` → `/inventory?tab=ink-registry` in [next.config.ts:66](next.config.ts).
- Cleaned the dead breadcrumb + route-label entries in [lib/breadcrumbs.ts:70](lib/breadcrumbs.ts), [components/app/sidebar/AppHeader.tsx:99](components/app/sidebar/AppHeader.tsx).

**Tags — merged into one tabbed page** ([app/(app)/settings/tags/](app/(app)/settings/tags/))
- `/settings/tags?tab=client` (default) → `<TagsManager />` for client-tag CRUD
- `/settings/tags?tab=style` → `<StyleTagsManager />`

- Permanent redirects: `/settings/studio/style-tags` → `/settings/tags?tab=style` and `/settings/studio/tags` → `/settings/tags` (safety net).
- Breadcrumb tab labels registered in [lib/breadcrumbs.ts](lib/breadcrumbs.ts:152) so the trail reads `Dashboard › Settings › Tags › Style`.
- [StyleTagPicker.tsx](components/shared/StyleTagPicker.tsx) "Add tags in settings" link retargeted.
- [DesignShowcase.tsx](app/(app)/dev/design/DesignShowcase.tsx) dev route listing updated.
